COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS 
18.09.2024 F.A. No. 162 of 2024 
Hon’ble Ritu Bahri, C.J.
Hon’ble Alok Kumar Verma, J. 
1. Mr. Piyush Garg, learned counsel for the 
appellant. 
2. Mr. Vishesh Srivastava, learned counsel 
for the respondent. 
3. The marriage of the parties was 
solemnized on 21.02.1999. They have one 
son and one daughter. They are living
separately since 2016. Respondent-husband 
has been granted divorce by the Family 
Court vide judgment dated 03.08.2024, on 
the ground that it is a dead marriage, and it 
amounts to mental cruelty as per the 
Supreme Court’s judgment rendered in 
Rakesh Raman Vs Smt. Kavita, 2023 
LiveLaw (SC) 353. 
4. Attempt can be made from an out of 
court settlement between the parties. 
5. Notice of motion.  6. Counsel appears and accepts notice on 
behalf of the respondent. 
7. List the matter on 02.11.2024. 
8. On that day, both the parties will 
remain present in person before the Court so 
that efforts can be made for making shared 
parenting plan. 
 
 (Alok Kumar Verma, J.) (Ritu Bahri, C.J.)
 18.09.2024 18.09.2024
Negi
